subject: Blanche reiterates national security concerns justify White House reporter ban
posts:
Defending press bans as national security.
Evidence: National security pretext, Judicial skepticism, Due process violation
#Aletheia #USPol

AG Todd Blanche claims barring critical media outlets from the White House protects national security.
Stated Judgement: (+0.6, 0.0) — Good Preference

Federal judges confirm hard passes were revoked without due process purely over negative reporting.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Punitive press exclusions are rebranded as national security to suppress scrutiny.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 4)

- Press Access Restrictions: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Punishes critical outlets under false pretenses.
- Legal Pretext: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Lacks evidentiary backing in court records.
Attorney General Todd Blanche defended barring outlets like CNN and Politico from the White House, claiming unfavorable news constitutes a national security risk.

The Poison:
Masking political retaliation and viewpoint discrimination as vital matters of national security erodes institutional trust.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (administrative press protocols) with WHO (critical journalists), weaponizing state power against political adversaries.

Social Physics Analysis:
The administration runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver, manufacturing a national security crisis to justify silencing critical press while projecting blame onto reporters.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Systemic friction increases as executive overreach collides with judicial oversight.

The Unavoidable Truth: Executive power cannot lawfully bypass constitutional due process to punish critical reporting.

The Unavoidable Lie: Unfavorable news coverage constitutes a direct threat to national security.

Alethekanon:
Rebranding political retaliation as national security is transparent authoritarian posturing. The judiciary correctly pierced this thin pretext.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch foundational democratic norms like a free press get sidelined for petty political grievances and manufactured fears.

Brothekanon:
Banning reporters just because you don't like their coverage isn't national security; it's just thin-skinned politics.

Spirithekanon:
"He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much." Luke 16:10 FAIL
Fabricating grand security threats over routine news coverage reveals a deeper fracture in institutional integrity.

Actual Article Body:
Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the White House’s reporter ban on Sunday, reiterating that it was implemented for national security purposes.

“Well, the president hasn’t denied access, that’s not the right way to describe it,” Blanche said while speaking with Martha Raddatz on ABC News’s This Week. She asked Blanche to justify the lack of TV pool coverage of President Donald Trump’s attendance at the Texas-Tennessee football game on Saturday after Trump barred CNN, Politico, and MSNOW from accessing the White House grounds on Monday.
